## CANDIDA GLABRATA
C. glabrata is often resistant to fluconazole and occasionally has some degree
of resistance to amphotericin. Higher doses of amphotericin are recommended due
to delayed killing effects against Candida glabrata.
## Duration of antimicrobial therapy
Duration of therapy is dependent upon location and severity of infection,
and response to therapy. Consult Infectious Diseases for more information.
## Preferred treatment
## Inpatient

Micafungin 100-150 mg IV q24h ($$$) [H,DI]
*150mg q24h for esophageal candidiasis, 100mg q24h for other indications
< OR >
## Alternative for susceptible isolates
Voriconazole 6mg/kg IV q12h for 2 doses, then 4mg/kg IV q12h ($$$$) [R,H,DI]
< OR >
Voriconazole 400 mg PO q12h for 2 doses, then 200 mg PO q12h ($$) [R,H,DI]
## Outpatient
Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS.
## Alternative for susceptible isolates
Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS for IV options
< OR >
Voriconazole 400 mg PO BID for 2 doses, then 200 mg PO BID ($$) [R,H,DI]
Non-VA order for above
